title: Students and activists protest wildfires and toxic haze in Jakarta
seoTitle: Jakarta protest against wildfires and toxic haze

tea.why: Protesters demonstrated against prolonged wildfires, toxic haze, corruption, and the government's response to the environmental crisis.
tea.want: Demonstrators demanded immediate action to extinguish fires, handle the climate crisis, lower the cost of living, and protect free expression.
tea.changed: Oct 20: Police evacuated six activists who scaled a Jakarta monument to display banners criticizing the government's handling of the crisis.

summary: On October 20, 2026, students and activists protested in Jakarta and several other Indonesian cities, coinciding with the second anniversary of President Prabowo Subianto's administration. Demonstrations were organized by groups including the University of Indonesia Student Executive Board, the All-Indonesia Student Executive Board, and the Komite Sadar coalition. Protesters railed against perceived government ineptitude and corruption in handling widespread wildfires and a toxic haze that has affected the region for weeks. In the capital, six Greenpeace activists climbed the Selamat Datang Monument to display banners demanding stronger climate action before being evacuated by authorities and taken to a medical facility. Protesters demanded immediate firefighting efforts, environmental protection, action against corruption, and relief from rising living costs.
organizers: University of Indonesia Student Executive Board
response: Central Jakarta police evacuated six activists who scaled a monument, taking them to a police medical facility after one appeared weak, according to police chief Reynold EP Hutagalung. Authorities also investigated how the monument was accessed.

updates.text: Six Greenpeace activists scaled Jakarta's Selamat Datang Monument and unfurled banners demanding climate action.
Authorities evacuated the six activists from the monument, taking them for medical checks after one required oxygen assistance.
Students and civil society groups held demonstrations in Jakarta and multiple other cities on the second anniversary of the administration.
